cards.title: Official ICT mentorship study entry
cards.note: The author's website links a core-content lesson on elements of a trade setup, hosted by the official YouTube channel. This verifies a study entry point, not lecture mastery or profitable implementation.

cards.title: ICT Episode 6 study topic
cards.note: The author's Episode 6 description identifies fair-value gaps, structure shifts, market efficiency and institutional order flow as lesson subjects. Full lecture content remains unreviewed.

cards.title: MT5 bar timestamps and UTC
cards.note: MetaQuotes documents tick and bar-open timestamps as UTC and advises aware UTC request datetimes. Preserve raw epochs; do not add a local-time offset twice. This API convention does not independently certify our captured provider clock or historical dataset.

cards.title: MT5 history availability
cards.note: The MT5 Python rate-range function returns only history available to the terminal's charts, constrained by the terminal's maximum-bars setting. A shorter response is not proof that absent intervals were market closures.

cards.title: Broker symbol specifications
cards.note: MetaQuotes symbol_info returns instrument properties together, including point, tick size/value, contract size, volume minimum/step and spread. Read the intended broker symbol's properties. Current values alone do not prove historical costs or equivalence to another NASDAQ product.

cards.title: MNQ futures are a distinct instrument
cards.note: CME describes Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures as $2 times the index, with a 0.25-index-point minimum tick. These futures specifications must not be assigned to broker-specific USTECH100M CFDs merely because both reference NASDAQ.

cards.title: FTMO 2-Step challenge objectives
cards.note: FTMO's 2-Step page specifies a 10% Challenge target, 5% Verification target and four minimum trading days. These are programme objectives, not expected returns. Confirm purchased account terms and stage before configuring a monitor.

cards.title: FTMO 2-Step daily loss reset
cards.note: The 2-Step daily equity floor is the balance at 00:00 CE(S)T minus 5% of initial simulated capital. Equity includes open P/L, swaps and commissions. The limit is recalculated at the next daily reset; floating losses still matter.

cards.title: FTMO 2-Step maximum loss floor
cards.note: FTMO's 2-Step maximum-loss equity floor is static at initial simulated capital minus 10%. Do not replace it with the different trailing-loss conventions used by other programmes.

cards.title: FTMO news rules depend on account stage
cards.note: FTMO's CFD FAQ exempts Challenge, Verification and Swing accounts from its selected-event execution restriction. Where the restriction applies, it includes stop-loss, take-profit and pending-order executions two minutes before and after the selected release. Forbidden practices still apply. This knowledge card never authorizes news trading.

cards.title: Personal risk ceiling by original account size
cards.note: The user selected at most 0.5% of original account size per entry and three entries per day, with zero allowed. Before costs, those ceilings are $25 on $5,000, $50 on $10,000 and $500 on $100,000. Headroom, existing exposure, costs and the risk engine may reduce them. These examples do not establish affordable lot sizes or authorize entries.

cards.title: Next-bar execution and conservative outcomes
cards.note: The existing research simulator waits until after the signal candle closes before a possible fill. It deducts specified round-trip costs and assumes stop first for ambiguous intra-bar paths. Its OHLC proxy cannot demonstrate actual broker fill quality. Use certified point units and avoid mixing legacy close-entry labels with next-open targets.

cards.title: Model training needs eligible evidence
cards.note: Training remains blocked on the six TIMEBASE_UNVERIFIED captures. Fit preprocessing inside chronological training folds, calibrate separately, purge overlapping outcome intervals and preserve an untouched final holdout. Synthetic fitting validates software, not market skill. A fitted text retriever is not a fitted BUY/SELL predictor.
